newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Standa in shr buyback, sees 1,200 lay-offs.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Standa in shr buyback, sees 1,200 lay-offs.

text.p: Italian retail chain Standa, a unit of opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi's Fininvest holding, said on Sunday it would launch a stock buyback from August 26 to September 19 as part of a restructuring plan.

The group announced last month that it intended to launch the buyback, known in Italian by the acronym OPA, for all ordinary and savings shares in Standa held by minority shareholders. It said in a prospectus that it expected to close 40 non-profitable stores and lay off 1,200 staff.
Fininvest has already said the operation for 5.35 million ordinary shares and 6.7 million savings shares would cost a total of 144.56 billion lire.
Each ordinary share will be valued at 20,000 lire and each savings share at 5,600 lire.

Fininvest said last month that the OPA was conditional on a minimum take-up rate which would give the media group 90 percent of the retail chain's share capital when added to those shares already in Fininvest's possession.
But it said it reserved the right to carry out the OPA even if the minimum level was not reached.

It said the operation also aimed to allow a relaunch of Standa's business some time in the future and a strengthening of its capital either through accords with other operators in the sector, reorganisation or mergers with non-listed companies in the Fininvest stable.
